analyzer.name: cbm
analyzer.description: Tree-sitter-based code knowledge graph server by DeusData

project_identification.description: DR CLI passes the project root as an absolute path via findProjectRoot(). The analyzer uses this path to establish a stable project identity for consistent indexing and caching across sessions.

analyzer.notes: Uses absolute path indexing for project identification. Ensures consistent graph generation and caching across multiple analysis runs within the same project.

Route.description: HTTP route maps to API operation with high confidence

Function.description: Function maps to application function; may be promoted to service via heuristics

Method.description: Class method maps to application function; may be promoted to service via heuristics

Module.description: Module (file/namespace) maps to application component with low confidence

Interface.description: In-code interface maps to an application data object. Tier-0 rules in extraction-heuristics.json take precedence: a Spring Data repository interface is data-store.accesspattern, an interface in generated client code or a component's props interface is not an element, and any other interface is narrowed to data object, application interface, application event or data-model object schema for the classifier to decide.

Type.description: Type alias or object type follows the Interface rules: an application data object unless generated or a component's props type.

Enum.description: Enumeration of values held in code follows the Interface rules: an application data object.

Struct.description: Plain struct maps to an application data object; one with receiver methods or an impl block behaves like a class (application component), which the classifier decides.

Trait.description: Behavioural contract implemented by types follows the Interface rules.

Table.description: A table CBM reads from SQL DDL (CREATE TABLE in schema and migration files) is a data-store collection (collectionType TABLE). A table declared in several files (one schema per SQL dialect, a migration and its schema) is one collection: extraction merges symbols of this label by name and records every file as a source location.

Image.description: A container image a Dockerfile builds from or copies from, or that a compose service or Kubernetes workload runs, is a technology artifact (artifactType container-image). CBM gives images no file; the element is matched by its name.

Chart.description: A Helm chart is a packaged deployment artifact: a technology artifact. Its artifactType is left to the agent. Not observed on the eval corpora.

Resource.description: An infrastructure object (a Kubernetes object, a compose service) maps by its kind, which CBM puts before the slash in its name (Deployment/petclinic, Service/db). Tier-0 rules in extraction-heuristics.json decide: a compose service or a Kubernetes Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet is a technology node (nodeType container), a Kubernetes Service a technology service, a Secret a technology artifact (artifactType configuration). Other kinds (ConfigMap, Ingress, Job, ...) are left to the agent with technology.node as the hint. A compose service declared in several compose files is one element: extraction merges symbols of this label by name.

Process.description: An external program the code or its scripts launch (the target of SPAWNS: git, node, a Dockerfile CMD) is system software the code depends on. A Tier-0 rule decides it; a program name computed at run time (<dynamic>) is not an element. Its softwareType is left to the agent. CBM gives processes no file; the element is matched by its name.

CALLS.description: A function calls another function: the caller depends on the callee
CALLS.implementation_note: Listed first: it is the call-graph default edge type for dr analyzer callers and callees. Creates a relationship only between functions that both survive classification. A call from a test case to the code it exercises (a component, function, process, interface, service, operation, object schema or access pattern) is the test testing it (testing.testcasesketch.tests.*); a call to a member with no element of its own counts as a call to its class, and from a test only when the test's file refers to that class (a USAGE or IMPORTS edge), because the index resolves a call by the member's name.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own. The edge itself passes the call-edge evidence gate (heuristic call_edge_evidence): below confidence 0.5 a name-only resolution needs corroboration

HANDLES.description: A function or method handles an HTTP route: the API operation for that route realizes the application function
HANDLES.implementation_note: CBM writes the edge handler → Route; the DR relationship runs from the operation to the function it realizes (api.operation.realizes.application.applicationfunction), so the direction is inverted. HANDLES names routes by path while Route nodes are named __route__METHOD__/path.

DEFINES_METHOD.description: A class defines a method: the application component is assigned the application function
DEFINES_METHOD.implementation_note: Deterministic. A controller class (application interface) defining its route handlers (application functions) creates no relationship here: the catalog has no interface-to-function structural triple, and the operation side comes from HANDLES.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

IMPORTS.description: Module or file import dependency: one application component uses another
IMPORTS.implementation_note: Only between application-layer elements (component to component, or a component or function to the data object a module defines); imports of external packages, and of anything else, stay traversal input (datastore detection reads them).

CALL_REFERENCE.description: A callable is used as a value (handler or callback registration): the registering function depends on it

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

DATA_FLOWS.description: A request crosses a route: data flows from the code that calls an HTTP or async route to the function that handles it
DATA_FLOWS.implementation_note: Not a local argument-to-parameter edge. CBM's route pass writes it only from the source of an HTTP_CALLS or ASYNC_CALLS edge into a Route to that Route's handler (its HANDLES source, or a handler reached through INFRA_MAPS), and skips it when the caller already CALLS the handler (src/pipeline/pass_route_nodes.c:746, CBM 0.12.1). Properties: via (the route's name), route (its qualified name), edge_type (HTTP_CALLS or ASYNC_CALLS), via_infra, handler_params and caller_args (the argument-to-parameter mapping). Not observed in the eval corpora, which have no in-repository client of their own routes. The fallback to depends-on is dropped: a caller depends on the operation, not on the code behind it.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

USAGE.description: A function or component uses a data structure without calling it: it accesses the data object
USAGE.implementation_note: The largest-reach edge (387 gold cards). Map only when the target was accepted as a data object (an Interface, Type, Enum or data class); usage of variables and anything else is traversal only. CBM rates USAGE as identifier use without a proven target, so confidence is low. A function or component using a data-model object schema (an entity class) accesses it, as it accesses a data object. CBM also records a workload or compose service referring to an artifact as USAGE: its container image (ref: image), or configuration it reads, such as a Secret through secretKeyRef. A technology.node to a technology.artifact is the node composing the artifact deployed to it (technology.node.composes.technology.artifact), a scoped-pair preference outside the data-object to_types.

WRITES.description: A function or component mutates a data structure's state: it accesses the data object
WRITES.implementation_note: Same targets as USAGE; writing is access, so the provider reading (serves) does not apply.

IMPLEMENTS.description: A class implements an interface that was classified as an application interface: the component provides that interface
IMPLEMENTS.implementation_note: Only when the implemented interface was accepted as application.applicationinterface. Implementing a data-object interface creates no relationship (the catalog has no component-to-dataobject structural triple, by design).

TESTS.description: A test function exercises a symbol: the test case sketch tests that component, function, interface, service, operation, object schema or access pattern
TESTS.implementation_note: From a test case (a test function Tier 0 classified as testing.testcasesketch) to the production symbol it exercises, when that symbol is an accepted element; calls into builtins, helpers and unclassified symbols create nothing.

TESTS_FILE.description: A test file covers a source file: the coverage target covers the component
TESTS_FILE.implementation_note: File-level counterpart of TESTS; same test pass.

ASYNC_CALLS.description: A function publishes to a queue or topic: it raises the application event the queue carries
ASYNC_CALLS.implementation_note: Inert (2026-11-12, #1080): the target is an async Route (__route__<transport>__..., e.g. __route__kafka__orders), and no node mapping or Tier-0 rule makes one an element: extraction reads only HTTP-method routes (parseRouteName), and the queue's Channel is unmapped. The mapping it stood for, application.applicationfunction.triggers.application.applicationevent (in the catalog since 2026-11-05), comes back once a rule classifies async Routes and Channels as application events.

LISTENS_ON.description: A function listens on a channel: the application event triggers the handler function
LISTENS_ON.implementation_note: Inert (2026-11-12, same cause as ASYNC_CALLS, #1080): CBM writes listener → Channel or async Route, and neither becomes an element. Once a rule classifies them as application events, map it inverted: application.applicationevent.triggers.application.applicationfunction. The interface-level reading waits on catalog addition 4.

SPAWNS.description: Code starts an external program: the system software serves the calling component
SPAWNS.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes caller → Process, the catalog has technology.systemsoftware.serves.application.applicationcomponent. Observed on CBM 0.12.1 (61 / 3 / 2 on dr-cli / fastapi / petclinic: git, node, bun, gh, claude and other programs the code or its scripts launch). Process maps to technology.systemsoftware since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9), so the edge creates a relationship when its caller is an application component; the catalog has no triple from an application function, a script or a Dockerfile (a Module with no card) to system software, so most observed SPAWNS still create none.

DEPENDS_ON.description: Infrastructure dependency between artifacts (charts, packages, base images) or system software
DEPENDS_ON.implementation_note: Infrastructure only: Helm chart dependencies, go.mod / requirements.txt to a Package, a Dockerfile to its base Images and an Image to its Dockerfile, compose depends_on and links (CBM 0.12.1; observed 0 / 12 / 1). Creates a relationship only between infrastructure elements (mapped since 2026-11-12, inventory step 9): compose depends_on between services is technology.node depends-on technology.node, an image on an image technology.artifact depends-on technology.artifact. A Dockerfile is a Module with no card, so the Dockerfile-to-image and image-to-Dockerfile edges create none, and an image is not linked to its base images through its Dockerfile.

INFRA_MAPS.description: A Kubernetes Service selects workloads: each workload node realizes the technology service
INFRA_MAPS.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes Service → workload. Observed on CBM 0.12.1 (petclinic 2: k8s Service to Deployment). Resource maps by kind since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9: Deployment to technology.node, Service to technology.technologyservice), so each edge creates technology.node realizes technology.technologyservice.

DEPLOYS.description: What deploys (a CI job, a script or Make rule, a Flux or Argo object, a Helm chart, a Terraform release) to what it deploys (manifests, Kubernetes objects, charts, images): the deploying artifact aggregates what it puts on a cluster
DEPLOYS.implementation_note: Not inverted: CBM writes deployer → deployed, and has no cluster node (README 0.12.1 'DEPLOYS'; src/pipeline/pass_k8s.c, pass_shell.c, pass_terraform.c, pass_operator.c, pass_ansible.c). Observed on CBM 0.12.1: petclinic's Module .github/workflows/deploy-and-test-cluster.yml DEPLOYS File k8s/db.yml. The deployer is a Module or Function (a workflow, script, Make rule, Go installer), a Resource (Flux or Argo object, Terraform resource) or a Chart; the deployed end is a File, Resource, Chart or Image. Resource, Chart and Image map to technology types since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9), so a Chart, Flux, Argo or Terraform deployer that is an element links to what it deploys; a CI workflow or script deployer is a Module or Function with no technology element, and a deployed manifest is a File, so petclinic's two edges still create none. from_types keeps a CI module or script function, which the node mapping places in the application layer, from linking to an artifact.

HTTP_CALLS.description: Outbound HTTP call to an API route. From a test case it is the test exercising that operation
HTTP_CALLS.implementation_note: Creates a relationship only from a test case (a symbol Tier 0 classified as testing.testcasesketch) to an operation: on CBM 0.12.1 almost every observed caller is test code (53 of 55 on fastapi, 81 of 86 on dr-cli). A production caller (application code consuming an operation) still creates none: that triple waits on catalog addition 7 (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md), queued in Context Studio. Extraction also reads this edge from test code that calls a served route by URL (MockMvc get("/owners/{ownerId}"), RestTemplate, supertest), which CBM has no edge for.

GRPC_CALLS.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

GRAPHQL_CALLS.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS. Emitted by CBM 0.12.1 (src/pipeline/pass_parallel.c, from a GraphQL client call to the operation's Route) but missing from its README edge list: emitted and undocumented, not binary-only. Proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

TRPC_CALLS.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS. Emitted by CBM 0.12.1 (src/pipeline/pass_parallel.c, from a tRPC client call to the procedure's Route) but missing from its README edge list: emitted and undocumented, not binary-only. Proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

INHERITS.description: Class or interface inheritance: the subclass specializes its parent
INHERITS.implementation_note: Only between two elements of the same type that the catalog lets specialize (object schemas, data objects, components, functions, ...): an entity class extending a mapped superclass. Inheriting from a class of another type, or from one that is not an element, creates nothing.

EXTENDS.implementation_note: In the CBM binary only (0.10.2 and 0.12.1), not in its documented vocabulary or any observed graph; kept for forward compatibility. INHERITS is the edge CBM emits for class extension.

OVERRIDE.implementation_note: specializes between functions; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 2); map once accepted. Also Kustomize patches in infrastructure.

EMITS.description: A function emits on a channel
EMITS.implementation_note: triggers an application event from a function or component; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

RAISES.description: A function raises an exception class
RAISES.implementation_note: Evidence for error-handling concerns; triggers an application event when the exception is a domain event, proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

THROWS.description: A method throws an exception class
THROWS.implementation_note: Same as RAISES: evidence for error-handling concerns; the triggers reading waits on catalog addition 3.

CONTAINS_FOLDER.implementation_note: composes between directory-level components; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 5); map once accepted.

CONNECTS_TO.implementation_note: depends-on from a node to a technology service; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 9); map once accepted.

DEFINES.implementation_note: Provenance: supplies source_reference.file for every element mapped from a symbol. Not a relationship between elements.

DECORATES.description: A decorator applies to a symbol
DECORATES.implementation_note: Evidence: decorator names feed the Tier-0 rules (extraction-heuristics.json) and the card. Decorator is not an element.

CONFIGURES.description: A symbol reads a config key, or a config key names a symbol
CONFIGURES.implementation_note: Evidence for security and APM concerns (EnvVar is not an element).

CONTAINS_FILE.implementation_note: Traversal only: the directory structure behind placement facts.

SEMANTICALLY_RELATED.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for Tier-0 clustering and duplicate detection.

SIMILAR_TO.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for duplicate detection.

FILE_CHANGES_WITH.description: Files that change together in history
FILE_CHANGES_WITH.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; evidence for component boundaries.

HAS_BRANCH.implementation_note: Provenance for source_reference; not a relationship.

REFERENCES_FILE.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

MENTIONS.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

READS.description: A function reads a field or variable
READS.implementation_note: The read half of WRITES: CBM 0.12.1 writes READS or WRITES for each member access (src/pipeline/pass_usages.c, pass_parallel.c), but its README edge list omits READS. Traversal input only for now: USAGE already links a reader to the type it reads, and the field or variable end is below element granularity.

SUPERSEDES.description: An architecture decision record supersedes an earlier one
SUPERSEDES.implementation_note: New in CBM 0.12.0: links ADR nodes, from the newer record to the one it supersedes. ADR has no node mapping (a decision record states intent, which the rules never decide). codebase_extract reads the edge to retire the older record: it gets no decision-record card, and an element sourced only from it is a candidate delete.

DIAGRAM_ARROW.description: An arrow between two elements of a diagram (Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz, D2, draw.io, Excalidraw)
DIAGRAM_ARROW.implementation_note: New in CBM 0.12.0 (src/pipeline/pass_diagrams.c): links DiagramElement nodes. A diagram states what someone drew, not what the code does: evidence for Tier 2's upper-layer inference at most.

CROSS_HTTP_CALLS.implementation_note: Federated extraction (2026-11-12, opt-in with codebase_index crossRepo; cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts). CBM 0.12.1 writes it from the caller to its own client Route, with target_project, target_function, target_file, url_path and (when the caller names the method) transport; the serving project gets a copy from the handler pointing back at one caller, which is skipped. It becomes a qualified cross-model reference on the caller's element (references field, @model/layer.type.name), not a relationship, so usage stays traversal_only. Predicate: the first catalog triple from the caller's type to the other model's api.operation (tests, triggers, references), else to the handler's element (flows-to, from application code, as DATA_FLOWS). An application caller has no triple to api.operation (catalog addition 7).

CROSS_GRPC_CALLS.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

CROSS_GRAPHQL_CALLS.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

CROSS_TRPC_CALLS.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

CROSS_ASYNC_CALLS.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (a Kafka producer and consumer in two fixture repositories linked as CROSS_CHANNEL, not this), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

CROSS_CHANNEL.implementation_note: Not mapped. CBM 0.12.1 writes it from the emitting or listening file (EMITS and LISTENS_ON have file sources) to its own Channel, with target_project, target_function (the other file's name), target_file, channel_name and transport, in both projects; the edge does not say which side emits. Neither side's Channel is an element (no rule makes one an application event yet, #1080), so there is no target for a reference. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out.

high.description: High confidence: mapping is reliable and well-supported by evidence

medium.description: Medium confidence: mapping is reasonably supported but may have ambiguity

low.description: Low confidence: mapping is tentative and may require manual verification

heuristics.name: min_fan_in
heuristics.description: Function/method with high fan-in (many callers) may be a service
heuristics.rule: If a function/method is called by 5+ other functions/methods, it exhibits service-like behavior and is eligible for promotion to applicationservice

heuristics.name: directory_match
heuristics.description: Element location in canonical service directories indicates service-level component
heuristics.rule: If element resides in directory matching service-level patterns, promote eligible functions to applicationservice

heuristics.name: naming_patterns
heuristics.description: Naming conventions indicate service-level components
heuristics.rule: If function/class name ends with service-indicating suffix (Service, Manager, Repository, etc.), promote eligible functions to applicationservice

heuristics.name: class_is_service
heuristics.description: Class structure and interface patterns indicate service behavior
heuristics.rule: If class implements interfaces, uses dependency injection, or has 3+ public methods, it may represent a service abstraction

heuristics.name: service_class_naming
heuristics.description: Class names following service patterns within classes indicate service methods
heuristics.rule: If method within service-named class uses CRUD or action-oriented prefix, it exhibits service operation behavior

heuristics.name: is_entry_point
heuristics.description: Functions that serve as entry points (main, handler, endpoint) indicate service potential
heuristics.rule: If function name or type suggests it serves as entry point (handler, endpoint, listener), it may represent service operation

heuristics.name: handles_route
heuristics.description: Functions that handle HTTP routes map directly to API operations
heuristics.rule: Function/method decorated with @Route, @Handler, or similar HTTP decorator maps to api.operation with high confidence

heuristics.name: datastore_detection
heuristics.description: Patterns and conventions that identify datastore-related elements (tables, schemas, migrations)
heuristics.rule: If element resides in datastore-related directories or files, or follows datastore naming conventions, identify it as a data-store collection or field, or a data-model object schema or schema property

heuristics.name: call_edge_evidence
heuristics.description: A call the index resolved by name alone, with low confidence and nothing to corroborate it, creates no relationship
heuristics.rule: CBM records how it resolved each CALLS edge (strategy, confidence, candidates) and an importance on functions, methods and classes. An edge at min_confidence or above is kept. Below it (unique_name 0.38, suffix_match 0.41 and under) about half are a name matched to the wrong definition, so the edge is kept only when the callee is called on a receiver and its name is unique in the project, when it is this.m() in the caller's own file, or when the caller's file imports the bare name from the callee's file or a directory index above it; never when the callee has no importance (a field or a variable). Run by cli/src/analyzers/call-evidence.ts; measured in docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md

heuristics.name: tier0_generated_code
heuristics.description: Symbols in generated client code are not elements
heuristics.rule: An interface, type, enum or function in a generated file (*.gen.ts, client/core/) is generator output, not a modelled element; the published API it was generated from is

heuristics.name: tier0_test_case_annotation
heuristics.description: A test-case annotation marks a test case
heuristics.rule: A method or function annotated as a test (JUnit @Test, @ParameterizedTest, @RepeatedTest, @TestFactory, @TestTemplate; a pytest mark) is one implemented test case, which the testing layer models as a test case sketch linked to it through source

heuristics.name: tier0_test_support_annotation
heuristics.description: Test setup, fixtures and test configuration are not elements
heuristics.rule: Setup and teardown methods (@BeforeEach, @AfterEach, @BeforeAll, @AfterAll), pytest fixtures and test-context annotations on classes (@SpringBootTest, @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, @ExtendWith, @TestConfiguration) support test cases; the testing layer has no element for them

heuristics.name: tier0_test_case_name
heuristics.description: A test-named function in a test file is a test case
heuristics.rule: A function or method in a Python, Go, Java or Kotlin test file whose name follows that runner's convention (pytest and unittest test_*, JUnit 3 testX, Go TestX) is one implemented test case. JavaScript and TypeScript are left out: their cases are anonymous it() and test() callbacks, and a named testX method there is a helper.

heuristics.name: tier0_test_file
heuristics.description: Other symbols in test files are test support, not elements
heuristics.rule: A helper, fixture, setup method or test class in a test file (tests/ and fixtures/ directories, test_*.py, conftest.py, *_test.go, *.test.ts, *.spec.ts, *Tests.java) supports the test cases. The testing layer has no element for it, and the production code under test belongs to the layer it implements. Test cases themselves are caught by the two rules before this one, except JavaScript and TypeScript ones: their anonymous it() and test() callbacks have no graph node, so extraction reads them from the test file's text and makes a test-case card for each.

heuristics.name: tier0_component_props
heuristics.description: A component's props type belongs to the component
heuristics.rule: An interface or type named ...Props in a .tsx or .jsx file declares a UI component's inputs and is part of that component, not an element of its own

heuristics.name: tier0_spring_data_repository
heuristics.description: Repository interfaces are data-store access patterns
heuristics.rule: An interface or class extending a Spring Data style repository (JpaRepository, CrudRepository, Repository) declares how the store is queried

heuristics.name: tier0_repository_query
heuristics.description: Query annotations mark data-store access patterns
heuristics.rule: A method annotated @Query or @Modifying is a declared store query

heuristics.name: tier0_route_handler
heuristics.description: Route-mapping decorators mark the application function that implements an API operation
heuristics.rule: A method or function decorated with a route mapping (@GetMapping, @RequestMapping, router.get, items_router.post, app.get, NestJS @Get, JAX-RS @GET, ...) is the application function that implements the route's API operation. The operation itself is the CBM Route node, and HANDLES links them as api.operation realizes application.applicationfunction.

heuristics.name: tier0_controller
heuristics.description: Controller annotations mark application interfaces
heuristics.rule: A class annotated @Controller or @RestController is the application interface its routes are served through

heuristics.name: tier0_persistent_entity
heuristics.description: Persistence annotations mark data-model object schemas
heuristics.rule: A class annotated @Entity, @Table, @MappedSuperclass, @Embeddable or @Document defines the shape of persisted data. Its table is a data-store collection the card builder derives (data-model.objectschema maps-to data-store.collection).

heuristics.name: tier0_sqlmodel_table
heuristics.description: SQLModel table classes are object schemas mapped to a table
heuristics.rule: A SQLModel class declared with table=True defines the shape of persisted data, like a JPA @Entity: it is a data-model object schema. Its table is a data-store collection that the card builder derives (data-model.objectschema maps-to data-store.collection), not the class itself.

heuristics.name: tier0_sqlmodel_schema
heuristics.description: SQLModel classes without a table are object schemas
heuristics.rule: A class deriving directly from SQLModel without table=True defines a data shape (request, response or base schema)

heuristics.name: tier0_otel_exporter_endpoint
heuristics.description: An OpenTelemetry exporter endpoint a deployment file sets is an exporter configuration
heuristics.rule: An OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_{TRACES,METRICS,LOGS}_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_JAEGER_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_ZIPKIN_ENDPOINT variable declared in a compose file, Kubernetes manifest or Dockerfile binds an exporter to a destination (OpenTelemetry SDK environment configuration). Only the endpoint key is the element: the protocol, headers, compression and exporter-selection keys configure the same exporter. A variable the code only reads has no file and no card

heuristics.name: tier0_envvar_other
heuristics.description: Other environment variables are not elements
heuristics.rule: A deployment file's other environment variables are configuration values, evidence for the elements that read them (security and APM concerns), not elements

heuristics.name: tier0_accessor
heuristics.description: Accessor and binder annotations are implementation details
heuristics.rule: A property accessor, serialization accessor or web-data binder hook is below element granularity

heuristics.name: tier0_spring_component
heuristics.description: Spring component stereotypes mark application components
heuristics.rule: A class annotated @Component or @SpringBootApplication is a deployable application component

heuristics.name: tier0_spring_service
heuristics.description: Spring service stereotype narrows to service or component
heuristics.rule: A class annotated @Service exposes application behaviour; it is the service or the component providing it

heuristics.name: tier0_compose_service
heuristics.description: A compose service is a technology node
heuristics.rule: A service in a Docker Compose file (CBM Resource Service/<name> in compose.yml, docker-compose.yml, compose.override.yml, ...) is a container the stack runs: a technology node. It is checked before the Kubernetes Service rule, which shares the name prefix.

heuristics.name: tier0_k8s_workload
heuristics.description: A Kubernetes workload is a technology node
heuristics.rule: A Kubernetes Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet runs containers: a technology node. Jobs, CronJobs and bare Pods are left to the agent.

heuristics.name: tier0_k8s_service
heuristics.description: A Kubernetes Service is a technology service
heuristics.rule: A Kubernetes Service is the stable endpoint through which the workloads it selects offer their capability: a technology service, which those workloads realize (INFRA_MAPS). Its serviceType is left to the agent.

heuristics.name: tier0_k8s_secret
heuristics.description: A Kubernetes Secret is a configuration artifact
heuristics.rule: A Kubernetes Secret is a configuration object deployed with the workloads that read it (credentials, keys, certificates): a technology artifact of artifactType configuration. The protected resource it guards, if the model needs one, is a security secure resource the agent models from intent, not from the manifest.

heuristics.name: tier0_dynamic_process
heuristics.description: A program named at run time is not an element
heuristics.rule: CBM records a launch whose program it cannot resolve statically as the Process <dynamic>; it names no program, so it is not an element

heuristics.name: tier0_process
heuristics.description: A launched program is system software
heuristics.rule: A program the code or its scripts start (SPAWNS: git, node, the server a Dockerfile's CMD runs) is third-party software the system depends on: technology system software. Its softwareType is left to the agent.

heuristics.name: tier0_ui_library
heuristics.description: Shared UI library directories hold library components
heuristics.rule: A component in a shared UI library directory (components/ui, packages/*/ui, design-system) is a reusable library component or a single action trigger, not a placed view

heuristics.name: tier0_file_route
heuristics.description: File-based route modules are views or routes
heuristics.rule: A module in a file-based routing directory (routes/ or pages/, or a Next.js app/ page, layout or route file) is reached by navigation: a view, a subview placed in a layout, or the route itself

heuristics.name: tier0_interface_default
heuristics.description: Other interfaces are application data objects or contracts
heuristics.rule: Any interface, type alias, enum or trait no earlier rule decided is an in-code data structure or contract: an application data object, application interface or application event (published schemas are data-model, but an in-code interface is not a published schema; design charter, 2026-10-25 relabelling); the classifier chooses, or says none

inference_rules.name: function-promotion-to-service
inference_rules.description: Qualified functions can be promoted to services via heuristic signals
inference_rules.pattern: applicationfunction + (min_fan_in >= 5 OR directory_match OR naming_patterns OR is_entry_point) => applicationservice

inference_rules.name: verify_scope_v1
inference_rules.description: Scope boundary rule: verify_role=primary applies only to api.operation (Route elements) in v1
inference_rules.pattern: verify_role: primary => api.operation only (excludes Function, Method, Class, Module)

filtering_rules.name: confidence_floor
filtering_rules.description: Filter mappings below confidence threshold to reduce noise

filtering_rules.name: test_code_exclusion
filtering_rules.description: Exclude test files and test-related code from mapping

deduplication_rules.name: semantic-duplicate-detection
deduplication_rules.description: Detect and merge semantically equivalent mappings
